section_summary: This section traces Allied debate over when to announce the Far Eastern Commission’s decision to review Japan’s new constitution, followed by preparations for the review itself in 1948. It includes correspondence with General MacArthur, legal opinions, press material, internal policy papers, and the opening pages of a copy of the constitution.

keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.title: Transmission of the Far Eastern Commission’s constitutional review decision
subfiles.about: Forwards the review policy and requests confidential consultation with the Supreme Commander about its public issuance.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the approved policy and asks for the Supreme Commander’s views on when and how to announce it.

subfiles.title: Draft minutes on provisions for review of the new Japanese constitution
subfiles.about: Records unanimous adoption of the review policy while postponing a decision on public announcement.
subfiles.summary: Australian and New Zealand representatives favor early announcement. McCoy explains United States concerns and secures agreement to consult the Supreme Commander before deciding when and how to issue the policy in Japan.

subfiles.title: Supreme Commander’s reply on publication of the review policy
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Opposes publicizing the review decision before experience with the constitution has accumulated.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur argues that the occupation already possesses review authority and that announcement would make the constitution appear imposed or threatened by Allied force. He recommends waiting at least until the first year of its operation has passed.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SWNCC papers to Tokyo
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to the Supreme Commander
subfiles.about: Encloses committee papers for the political adviser’s information.
subfiles.summary: Sends SWNCC 228/12, SWNCC 236/30, and a status corrigendum.

subfiles.title: SWNCC transmittal of Directive Serial No. 66
subfiles.about: Sends copies of the directive transmitted to the Supreme Commander.
subfiles.summary: Provides three copies of Directive Serial No. 66 for the Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Directive on issuance of the constitutional review decision
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs formal communication of the review policy to Japan’s government while public announcement remains under consideration.
subfiles.summary: Orders formal notice to Japan’s government; leaves the timing of public announcement unresolved.

subfiles.title: Filing of Directive Serial No. 66 with the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Files a certified copy of the directive concerning issuance of the review policy.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a certified copy of Directive Serial No. 66 for Commission filing.

subfiles.title: Guidance to the United States member on announcement policy
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Sends the United States position on announcing the constitutional review provisions.
subfiles.summary: Instructs the member to follow the enclosed United States policy statement.

subfiles.title: United States policy toward announcement of review provisions
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Conditions publication on consultation with MacArthur and consistency with United States policy.
subfiles.summary: Withholds agreement to publication until consultation with MacArthur and a favorable policy judgment.

subfiles.title: Opinion on laws implementing the Japanese constitution
subfiles.about: Examines the current Diet’s authority to enact laws needed to implement the new constitution.
subfiles.summary: Snow concludes that the new constitution permits preparatory legislation by the current Diet, including succession and election laws. He notes that each law’s substantive consistency with the constitution still requires separate examination.

subfiles.title: Revised opinion on implementing laws
subfiles.about: Restates the opinion that the existing Diet may enact preparatory laws under the new constitution.
subfiles.summary: This revised opinion cites constitutional provisions on the throne, elections, continuity of office, and judicial review. It leaves examination of individual implementing laws for later.

subfiles.title: Publication of FEC policy decision on constitutional review
subfiles.about: Urges consideration of early publication despite MacArthur’s objections.
subfiles.summary: Reviews the dispute, a press leak, and the argument that further secrecy risks accusations of bad faith.

subfiles.title: Recommendation on publication of the FEC review decision
subfiles.about: Recommends publication outside Japan while respecting MacArthur’s objection to publication within Japan.
subfiles.summary: Recommends against requiring publication in Japan but supports release elsewhere.

subfiles.title: McCoy forwards Plimsoll’s letter
subfiles.about: Forwards an Australian argument for informing Japanese voters about the planned review.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Plimsoll’s letter for consideration in the publication debate.

subfiles.title: Plimsoll on informing voters before Diet elections
subfiles.about: Argues that voters should know the next Diet may review the constitution.
subfiles.summary: Plimsoll urges announcement before the election campaign so voters can consider the Diet’s possible constitutional role.

subfiles.title: SWNCC approval of revised announcement policy
subfiles.about: Reports approval of amended SWNCC 228/13 and requests distribution of its conclusion.
subfiles.summary: Sends the approved paper for transmission to the United States Commission member.

subfiles.title: Decision amending SWNCC 228/13
subfiles.about: Directs substitution of the revised policy page.
subfiles.summary: Records committee approval and instructs holders to replace the superseded page.

subfiles.title: Policy toward announcement of constitutional review provisions
subfiles.about: Sets the United States position on release of the Far Eastern Commission’s review decision outside Japan.
subfiles.summary: The revised conclusion withdraws the United States objection to publication outside Japan, provided release follows confirmation of SCAP’s receipt by 48 hours. Appendices reproduce the review policy and argue that leaks, parliamentary questions, and delayed disclosure favor publication. They also contend that advance notice would support democratic implementation of the constitution.

subfiles.title: Transmission of United States announcement position
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Sends the approved United States position on announcement of the review provisions.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the conclusion of SWNCC 228/13 as guidance.

subfiles.title: Commission decision to release the review policy outside Japan
subfiles.about: Requests urgent notice to SCAP of the Commission’s decision to release the policy to the press outside Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports the Commission’s vote and the 48-hour interval after confirmation of receipt in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Suggested message to MacArthur on press release
subfiles.about: Notifies MacArthur of the release decision and requests acknowledgment of receipt.
subfiles.summary: Drafts a message establishing the 48-hour press release interval.

subfiles.title: Request to transmit the Commission’s press release decision
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the release decision to SCAP and acknowledgment of its receipt.
subfiles.summary: Passes the Commission’s decision and the United States 48-hour condition to the Joint Chiefs.

subfiles.title: Request for a copy of Japan’s constitution
subfiles.about: Requests a complete text of the Constitution of Japan for library files.
subfiles.summary: Asks Borton to supply a copy of the constitution.

subfiles.title: Reply supplying Japan’s constitution
subfiles.about: Responds to the newspaper library’s request for the constitution.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a copy of the Constitution of Japan.

subfiles.title: Illegible file notation
subfiles.about: A short handwritten or poorly recognized filing notation.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR does not establish its purpose.

subfiles.title: Reply to Hall enclosing the Constitution of Japan
subfiles.about: Supplies a copy of the constitution in response to a January request.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Publication 2836, the Constitution of Japan.

subfiles.title: Interpretation of Japan’s constitution by an occupation spokesman
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Questions a SCAP spokesman’s public criticism of reporting the Katayama Cabinet’s resignation to the Emperor.
subfiles.summary: The adviser describes the spokesman’s interpretation of the Emperor’s constitutional role. He warns that an interpretation pronounced by occupation authority could encourage Japanese reliance on external fiat rather than constitutional government.

subfiles.title: Nippon Times report on alleged misuse of the Emperor system
subfiles.about: Reports Guy J. Swope’s criticism of the Cabinet’s report of its resignation to the Emperor.
subfiles.summary: Swope calls for an amendment to Article 7 to prevent expansion of the Emperor’s ceremonial role.

subfiles.title: Despatch enclosing a constitution anniversary statement
subfiles.about: Encloses Sebald’s statement for the first anniversary of the constitution’s enforcement.
subfiles.summary: Sends an approved anniversary statement intended for publication in the Yomiuri Shimbun.

subfiles.title: Statement on the first anniversary of Japan’s new constitution
subfiles.about: Urges Japanese citizens to preserve constitutional rights and democratic freedom.
subfiles.summary: Praises rights guaranteed by the constitution and warns against leaders who would erode them.

subfiles.title: Illegible assistant secretary note
subfiles.about: A short note whose substance cannot be recovered from the OCR.
subfiles.summary: Only the Assistant Secretary letterhead and fragments are legible.

subfiles.title: McCoy urges preparation for constitutional review
subfiles.about: Calls attention to the Commission’s review deadline and asks for a United States study of possible amendments.
subfiles.summary: McCoy notes that the Commission’s review period ends in May 1949 and that Diet or Commission members may propose amendments. He asks State to prepare a position on revision.

subfiles.title: Saltzman acknowledges McCoy’s review request
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the request for a United States position on constitutional review.
subfiles.summary: Says steps are being taken to determine the United States position.

subfiles.title: Copy of McCoy’s letter on the review deadline
subfiles.about: Repeats McCoy’s request for a departmental study before the Far Eastern Commission’s review.
subfiles.summary: This duplicate copy describes the May 1949 deadline, possible amendment proposals, and the need for an informed United States position.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Australian delegate on constitutional review
subfiles.about: Records Bullock’s proposed consultation with SCAP and Australia’s preference for a harmonious review.
subfiles.summary: Bullock supplies a draft message; Dunning questions its assertion that the Commission must review the constitution.

subfiles.title: Request for a State Department position on review
subfiles.about: Assigns preparation of a statement addressing McCoy’s questions about constitutional review.
subfiles.summary: Requests a coordinated statement grounded in current United States policy and the Commission commitment.

subfiles.title: Australian draft consultative message to SCAP
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Seeks SCAP’s views on the constitution’s operation and progress of Japanese discussion.
subfiles.summary: Proposes consulting SCAP before the Commission’s review begins.

subfiles.title: Instruction to index and file a document
subfiles.about: Requests filing of an unrecorded original found during file cleaning.
subfiles.summary: Asks that the original be indexed and filed.

subfiles.title: Snow forwards a draft review of Japan’s constitution
subfiles.about: Sends a draft constitutional review for consideration in forming a United States position.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a draft review, including comparisons with United States constitutional practice.

subfiles.title: Draft chapter-by-chapter review of Japan’s constitution
subfiles.about: Examines the constitution’s institutions and rights, often against United States constitutional practice.
subfiles.summary: The draft discusses the Emperor’s ceremonial position and questions whether Article 9 effectively restrains future rearmament. It also raises concerns about criminal procedure, legislative quorums, treaty approval, impeachment, judicial independence, and local legislation. Several pages are severely degraded in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Australia’s proposed SCAP consultation
subfiles.about: Records United States objections to an immediate broad request for SCAP’s views on constitutional review.
subfiles.summary: Allison calls the proposed message premature, and Bullock agrees to postpone it. Participants suggest that delegations study specific issues first and use the Commission’s committee; they favor minimal changes that account for Japanese reactions.

subfiles.title: Proposed United States position on FEC review
subfiles.about: Assesses possible Commission review, amendments, and a referendum under United States occupation policy.
subfiles.summary: Dunning notes the United States commitment to Commission review while arguing that Japanese people should lead any amendments. The paper invokes NSC 13’s emphasis on assimilating existing reforms, warns against externally imposed changes, and recommends opposing a referendum. Its recommendations begin on the final page but are cut off.

subfiles.title: Instructions to the United States member on constitutional review
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Directs support for a prompt, quiet review concluding that Japan’s constitution meets Commission requirements.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman authorizes opposition to further investigation, a referendum, or Commission proposals for amendment. He argues that Japan’s people should decide when to amend their constitution and that outside intervention would undermine its legitimacy.

subfiles.title: Minutes of meeting on the United States review position
subfiles.about: Records agreement on a quiet review and discussion of whether to reject all possible amendments in advance.
subfiles.summary: Participants retain flexibility to consider a compelling proposal while planning arguments against unnecessary revision.

subfiles.title: Proposed instructions for the United States Commission member
subfiles.from: Far Eastern and Northeast Asian Affairs officers
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Proposes a quiet review and assigns responsibility for future amendments to the Japanese people.
subfiles.summary: The draft also proposes rejecting Commission amendments or further action.

subfiles.title: Constitution of Japan, opening pages
subfiles.about: Reproduces the preamble and opening articles of Japan’s constitution.
subfiles.summary: The text opens with popular sovereignty and peace, then sets out the Emperor’s constitutional role, renunciation of war, and the first provisions on fundamental rights. It continues beyond this section.
